description: A graphql-middleware plugin for schema-agnostic CASL permission rules on GraphQL resolvers, declared per type/field in a PermissionsMap and enforced before each resolver runs.
rules: The library is schema-agnostic: subject names and condition types are derived from the consumer's generated Resolvers / ResolversTypes. Never hardcode domain type names in the library core.

All public exports come from src/index.ts: runtime helpers (createGraphQLAbility, buildGraphQLAbility, createCan, createTyped, subjectsOf, rule, and/or/not/chain/race, accept, deny, applyPermissions, resolvePermissions, accessibleBy, Actions) plus type helpers (PermissionsMap, Rule, CheckableRule, GraphQLAbility, SubjectName, SubjectMap, Subjects, ArgsOf, etc.). subjectsOf<SubjectMap>() returns a Subject namespace of typo-proof subject names with nothing to declare; it is optional, because every API taking a subject name also accepts the bare string literal and type-checks it identically. createSubjects is deprecated in its favour but still exported.

Abilities are built with createGraphQLAbility<SubjectMap>(), which returns a CASL AbilityBuilder whose conditions are type-checked against each subject's fields and whose build() applies __typename subject detection. Consumers tag plain objects with createTyped() rather than CASL's subject(). Conditions use CASL's mongo-query operators and are plain JSON, so rules can be stored in a database and rehydrated with buildGraphQLAbility.

createCan(getAbility, isAuthenticated, buildSubject?, options?) returns a requireCan(action, subject, getSubjectData?) rule builder bound to the consumer's context and ability builder; getSubjectData reads condition values from the resolver args and parent, and getAbility(context) is memoized per request. requireCan.onResult authorizes the value the resolver returned instead of the args; requireCan.fields decides every field of a type from the ability's field lists.

rule(check) wraps a predicate returning true | false | string | Error into a combinable rule; and/or/not/chain/race compose combinable rules; wrap(...rules) nests ANY rules as middleware (each receives the next as its resolve) and is the only way to compose onResult or scopeArgs, returning a plain Rule that is never itself a combinator operand. accept is the always-pass primitive, deny the always-fail one. A failed authentication check throws 'Not authenticated'; a failed ability check throws 'Forbidden', or the matched rule's cannot(...).because(...) reason.

applyPermissions(schema, permissions, options?) validates the map against the runtime schema (throwing PermissionsError, which aggregates every problem) and applies it via graphql-middleware. Options: fallbackRule, '*' wildcards in either position, fallbackError, allowExternalErrors (defaults to true, the opposite of graphql-shield), debug, and maskDenials. Only denials are masked or reworded — a rule's own bug and a resolver error keep their own errors. resolvePermissions is the same layer without the graphql-middleware binding, for other integrations.

accessibleBy(ability, action, subject, adapter?) folds the ability's rules into a query filter so a list resolver fetches only accessible rows; null means deny-all and {} means no restriction. A FilterAdapter is either a SkeletonAdapter (rule/and/or/everything — conditions pass through verbatim) or a LeafAdapter (leaf/not/and/or/everything — each comparison is delivered as { path, operator, value }).

scopeArgs(requireCan, action, subject, options) is the OPTIONAL subpath export @vantreeseba/graphql-casl/scoping. It is a Rule that rewrites a field's filter argument (options.into, default 'where') with the ability's filter, for generated CRUD resolvers there is no seam to edit. It ANDs the scope onto the client's filter, leaves args untouched when the ability restricts nothing, and throws Forbidden on deny-all unless onDenyAll is 'nothing'. It is not combinable and is not a gate — pair it with fallbackRule, or compose it with wrap(). Injected arguments bypass GraphQL input coercion, so applyPermissions checks that `into` names a real argument of the field.

useGraphQLCasl(options) is the OPTIONAL subpath export @vantreeseba/graphql-casl/envelop, an envelop Plugin. It enforces the same PermissionsMap by wrapping resolvers as envelop hands them over instead of wrapping the schema with graphql-middleware — for Apollo Server 4+, federated gateways, and dynamically swapped schemas. options.permissions is the map; every other key is an ApplyPermissionsOptions field. It calls resolvePermissions, so wildcard precedence, fallbackRule coverage, error control and masking are identical. The map is validated when the schema arrives, not on the first query; introspection is never guarded; fields with no resolver of their own are guarded too; each field is wrapped once. Use it OR applyPermissions, never both — two layers would run every rule twice.

Stack: TypeScript 5 strict, ESM only, Vitest for tests, Biome for lint/format. No runtime dependencies — @casl/ability >=6, graphql >=16, and graphql-middleware >=6 are peer deps; @envelop/core >=5 and @envelop/on-resolve >=7 are OPTIONAL peer deps, needed only by the /envelop entry point. Optional entry points: @vantreeseba/graphql-casl/scoping (scopeArgs) and @vantreeseba/graphql-casl/envelop (useGraphQLCasl). Sibling package: @vantreeseba/graphql-casl-codegen (codegen plugin).
Use Conventional Commits; commits drive automated semantic-release publishing (feat = minor, fix = patch, BREAKING CHANGE = major).
